result.title: EgoPass-Bench: Identifying Objects That May Affect the Wearer's Passage in Egocentric Video
result.summary: Understanding an egocentric environment requires reasoning about how surrounding entities affect the observer's actions. Existing evaluations of multimodal foundation models (MFMs) examine observer localization, motion trajectories, and action feasibility, but leave the discovery and interpretation of evolving observer-entity interactions insufficiently assessed. We introduce EgoPass-Bench, a benchmark for observer-relative interaction understanding in real-world egocentric video. EgoPass-Bench comprises 284 manually reviewed evaluation clips recorded using Ray-Ban Meta (Gen 2) smart glasses and 2,201 distinct questions across five tasks assessing motion perception, interaction judgments about specified entities, and relevant-entity discovery without target cues. Our evaluation of eight frame-based and six native-video configurations reveals a pronounced discrepancy between motion perception and interaction understanding. The strongest evaluated model, GPT-6 Astra, correctly recognizes object motion in 91.37% of 394 comparisons involving the same targets, but correctly identifies changes in passage constraints in only 66.50%. Across all 574 entity-discovery questions, it trails the two-person human baseline by $23.65 \pm 7.45$ percentage points (paired 95% CI), while exceeding the always-empty baseline (36.76%) by at least 18.9 percentage points. Further analysis reveals frequent inclusion of entities that neither pose a plausible physical conflict nor constrain passage, showing that accurate motion recognition does not ensure reliable relevant-entity discovery.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 EgoPass-Bench：以智能眼镜采集的 284 段第一视角片段和 2201 个问题，从运动感知、指定实体的交互判断到无目标提示的相关实体发现三个层面，评估多模态基础模型能否找出影响佩戴者通行的实体。
AI.relevance_reason: 该基准诊断「能识别物体运动却选不准通行约束实体」的失败模式，与 VLM 推理中的视觉证据筛选、任务必要几何与实体关系是否保留在内部状态相关，可供核查其错误类型与评价设计是否适用于 LVR 研究。
